summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, with hands-on experience building and testing robotic and autonomous-vehicle software systems in C++ and Python. Designed and validated a collision-avoidance control stack for a simulated autonomous vehicle, achieving zero collisions across multi-agent traffic scenarios, and debugged multi-sensor robotic hardware integrations end-to-end. Comfortable across the software development life cycle -- design, verification, and validation -- coordinating with hardware component teams to resolve integration issues.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and Bluetooth to translate hand motion into hardware control commands via Python, debugging and resolving sensor jitter through calibration.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI application using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization, using GitLab for version control within a structured software development workflow.

experience.title: AI/ML Intern
bullets: Built preprocessing and training pipelines in PyTorch for a document-understanding transformer, improving validation accuracy from 55% to 93% through structured software testing, problem solving, and iteration.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided robotic pick-and-place system integrating Jetson-deployed, TensorRT-optimized YOLO perception (5.2x speedup) and dual ToF range sensors for contact-aware, collision-safe grasping.

Resolved 11 hardware/software integration failures (false-positive camera detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture), achieving 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) through end-to-end debugging and verification of a real-time robotic system.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics in C++ on Arduino, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection for safe object handling.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving in CARLA
bullets: Built an adaptive autonomous-vehicle control stack with lane-following and waypoint fallback, integrating camera-based YOLO object detection and lane-segmentation perception models.
Validated the collision-avoidance control stack in a simulated town with 30 vehicles and 10 pedestrians, achieving zero collisions and correct traffic-signal compliance across multiple laps.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Derived DH tables and forward kinematic chains for a 6-DoF UR5e and 5-DoF AL5B, validating results against MoveIt and RViz URDF models in ROS 2.
Planned collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on a physical UR5e; verified AL5B repeatability at under 2mm over 10 trials through systematic testing.
